summary: If a father married off his young daughter and she was later divorced or widowed, her kesubah money belongs to her. If she only had erusin, it belongs to her father.

chunks.st: the payment specified in her marriage contract, even from her second husband, is his, i.e., it belongs to the father.

chunks.st: However, if her father married her off and her husband divorced her,

summary: A girl who became Jewish together with her mother, and later did a very serious sin as a kallah, gets a different punishment than a girl born Jewish. It depends on when she was born.

chunks.stMore: not stoning, the method of execution that would be employed had she been born Jewish.

words.note: A kind of death penalty of beis din.

summary: A father has rights over his young daughter: making her kiddushin, what she finds, what she earns, and her vows. A husband has even more rights, and he must feed her, ransom her and bury her.

chunks.en: A father is in charge of his daughter's kiddushin,
chunks.st: A father has authority over his daughter with regard to her betrothal

chunks.en: with money, with a document, or with the third way of kiddushin.
chunks.st: through money, through a marriage document, or through intercourse.

chunks.en: He gets what she finds,
chunks.st: Likewise, a father is entitled to items she has found,

chunks.en: and what she earns with her hands,
chunks.st: and to her earnings,

chunks.en: and he can cancel her vows.
chunks.st: and to effect the nullification of her vows,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a father may nullify his daughter’s vows.

chunks.en: He receives her get for her,
chunks.st: And he accepts her bill of divorce
chunks.stMore: on her behalf if she is divorced from betrothal before she becomes a grown woman.

chunks.en: but he does not eat the fruits of her property while she is alive.
chunks.st: And although he inherits her property when she dies, e.g., property she inherited from her mother’s family, he does not consume the produce of her property during her lifetime.

chunks.he: נִשֵּׂאת, יָתֵר עָלָיו הַבַּעַל שֶׁאוֹכֵל פֵּרוֹת בְּחַיֶּיהָ,
chunks.en: When she marries, the husband has more than him, since he eats the fruits of her property while she is alive.
chunks.st: If the daughter married, the husband has more rights and obligations than her father had before the marriage, as he consumes the produce of her property during her lifetime,

chunks.en: He must feed her,
chunks.st: and he is obligated to provide her sustenance,

chunks.en: ransom her if she is captured, and bury her.
chunks.st: her redemption if she is captured, and her burial upon her death.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: Even the poorest man in Yisrael
chunks.st: Even the poorest man of the Jewish people

chunks.en: must have at least two flutes and a woman who cries at her funeral.
chunks.st: may not provide fewer than two flutes and a lamenting woman,
chunks.stMore: which it was customary to hire for a funeral, as these too are included in the duties of burial.

summary: A kallah stays under her father's say until she is brought to her husband for the chuppah. It depends on whose messengers handed her over to whom.
stIntro: Even after she is betrothed, a daughter

chunks.en: She is always under her father's say
chunks.st: is always under her father’s authority

chunks.en: until she comes under her husband's say at the chuppah.
chunks.st: until she enters her husband’s authority in marriage via the wedding canopy.

chunks.en: If the father handed her to the husband's messengers,
chunks.st: If the father delivered his daughter to the husband’s messengers
chunks.stMore: to bring her to her husband and the wedding canopy,

chunks.en: she is under her husband's say.
chunks.st: once she has been handed over she is under the husband’s authority.

chunks.en: If the father went with the husband's messengers,
chunks.st: However, if the father went with the husband’s messengers,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁהָלְכוּ שְׁלוּחֵי הָאָב עִם שְׁלוּחֵי הַבַּעַל,
chunks.en: or the father's messengers went with the husband's messengers,
chunks.st: or if the father’s messengers went with the husband’s messengers,

chunks.en: she is still under her father's say.
chunks.st: she is still under the father’s authority,
chunks.stMore: as he has not fully delivered her to the husband’s messengers.

chunks.en: If the father's messengers handed her to the husband's messengers,
chunks.st: If her father sent her with his own messengers and the father’s messengers delivered the woman to the husband’s messengers,

chunks.en: she is under her husband's say.
chunks.st: from that moment onwards she is under her husband’s authority.

summary: A father does not have to feed his daughter. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah taught that daughters are fed from their father's property only after he dies, just as sons inherit only after he dies.

chunks.en: A father does not have to feed his daughter.
chunks.st: A father is not obligated to provide his daughter’s sustenance.

chunks.he: זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן
chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben
chunks.st: This exposition was expounded by Rabbi Elazar ben

chunks.en: Azaryah taught this before the Sages in the vineyard in Yavneh:
chunks.st: Azarya before the Sages in the vineyard of Yavne:

chunks.en: The sons inherit, and the daughters are fed.
chunks.st: Since the Sages instituted that after the father’s death, the sons inherit the sum of money specified in their mother’s marriage contract, and the daughters are sustained
chunks.stMore: from their father’s estate, these the two halakhot are equated:

chunks.en: Just as the sons inherit
chunks.st: Just as the sons inherit

chunks.en: only after the father dies,
chunks.st: only after the father’s death, not during his lifetime,

chunks.en: so too the daughters are fed
chunks.st: so too, the daughters are sustained from his property

chunks.en: only after their father dies.
chunks.st: only after their father’s death.

summary: Even if a husband did not write a kesubah, his wife still gets the set amount, because beis din made it a rule. All his property stands behind the kesubah even if he did not write so.

chunks.en: If he did not write a kesubah for her,
chunks.st: did not write a marriage contract for his wife,

chunks.en: a maiden collects two hundred,
chunks.st: a virgin collects two hundred dinars

chunks.en: and a widow one hundred,
chunks.st: and a widow one hundred dinars upon divorce or the husband’s death,

chunks.en: because it is a rule of beis din.
chunks.st: because it is a stipulation of the court that a wife is entitled to these amounts.

chunks.en: If he wrote for her:
chunks.st: If he wrote in her marriage contract that she is entitled to

chunks.he: שָׂדֶה שָׁוֶה מָנֶה תַּחַת מָאתַיִם זוּז,
chunks.en: a field worth one hundred instead of two hundred zuz,
chunks.st: a field worth one hundred dinars instead of the two hundred dinars to which she is actually entitled,

chunks.en: and he did not write for her,
chunks.st: and he did not additionally write for her:

chunks.he: כָּל נְכָסִים דְּאִית לִי אַחֲרָאִין לִכְתֻבְּתִיךְ,
chunks.en: All my property stands behind your kesubah,
chunks.explain: She can collect from any of his things.
chunks.st: All property I have shall serve as a guarantee for the payment of your marriage contract,

chunks.en: he must pay anyway, because it is a rule of beis din.
chunks.st: he is nevertheless obligated to pay the full two hundred dinars; and he cannot say that she should take only a mortgaged field for payment of her marriage contract, as it is a stipulation of the court
chunks.stMore: that all his property is held as surety for the entire sum.

summary: A husband must ransom his wife if she is captured and take her back, even if he did not write this in the kesubah. If he is a Kohen and cannot take her back, he must still bring her home.

chunks.en: If he did not write for her:
chunks.st: he did not write for her in the marriage contract:

chunks.he: אִם תִּשְׁתַּבָּאִי אֶפְרְקִנָּךְ וְאוֹתְבִנָּךְ לִי לְאִנְתּוּ,
chunks.en: If you are captured, I will ransom you and take you back as my wife,
chunks.st: If you are taken captive I will redeem you and restore you to me as a wife,

words.en: and I will take you back

chunks.en: or for a Kohen's wife: I will bring you back to your hometown,
chunks.explain: A Kohen's wife who was captured may not go back to him.
chunks.st: and in the case of a priestess, i.e., the wife of a priest, who is prohibited to return to her husband if she has intercourse with another man even if she is raped, if he did not write: I will return you to your native province,

words.en: and for a Kohenes (a Kohen's wife)

chunks.en: he must do it anyway, because it is a rule of beis din.
chunks.st: he is nevertheless obligated to do so, as it is a stipulation of the court.

summary: A husband must ransom his wife if she is captured, and he cannot get out of it by divorcing her. But he may divorce her and pay her kesubah instead of paying for her doctor.

chunks.en: If she was captured, he must ransom her.
chunks.st: was taken captive, her husband is obligated to redeem her.

chunks.en: And if he said,
chunks.st: And if he said:

chunks.en: Here is her get and her kesubah,
chunks.st: I hereby give my wife her bill of divorce and the payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: let her ransom herself,
chunks.st: and let her redeem herself,

chunks.en: he is not allowed.
chunks.st: he is not permitted
chunks.stMore: to do so, as he already obligated himself to redeem her when he wrote the marriage contract.

chunks.en: If she got sick, he must heal her.
chunks.st: If his wife was struck with illness, he is obligated to heal her, i.e., to pay for her medical expenses.

chunks.en: If he said, Here is her get and her kesubah,
chunks.st: In this case, however, if he said: I hereby give my wife her bill of divorce and the payment of her marriage contract,

chunks.en: let her heal herself, he is allowed.
chunks.st: and let her heal herself, he is permitted to do so.

summary: The sons of a woman inherit her kesubah money, on top of their share with their brothers from other mothers. This is a rule of beis din even if it was not written.

chunks.en: If he did not write for her:
chunks.st: did not write for her in her marriage contract:

chunks.en: The sons that you will have from me
chunks.st: Any male children you will have from me

chunks.en: will inherit the money of your kesubah, more
chunks.st: will inherit the money of your marriage contract in addition

chunks.en: than their share with their brothers,
chunks.st: to their portion of the inheritance that they receive together with their brothers,

chunks.en: he must do it anyway, because it is a rule of beis din.
chunks.st: he is nevertheless obligated as though he had written it, as it is a stipulation of the court
chunks.stMore: and therefore takes effect even if it is not explicitly stated.

summary: The daughters of a man who died are fed from his property until they get married. This is a rule of beis din even if it was not written.
stIntro: Likewise, if he omitted from the marriage contract the sentence: Any

chunks.en: The daughters that you will have from me
chunks.st: female children you will have from me

chunks.st: will sit in my house and be sustained

chunks.en: from my property until they marry men,
chunks.st: from my property until they are taken by men, i.e., until they are married,

chunks.en: he must do it anyway, because it is a rule of beis din.
chunks.st: he is nevertheless obligated as though he had written it, as it too is a stipulation of the court.

summary: A widow may live in her husband's house and be fed from his property. In Yerushalayim and the Galil this lasted as long as she was a widow; in Yehudah the heirs could pay her kesubah and send her off.
stIntro: Similarly, if he omitted from the marriage contract the clause:

chunks.he: אַתְּ תְּהֵא יָתְבָא בְּבֵיתִי וּמִתְּזָנָא מִנִּכְסַי,
chunks.en: You will live in my house and be fed from my property
chunks.st: You will sit in my house and be sustained from my property

chunks.en: all the days that you are a widow in my house,
chunks.st: all the days you live as a widow in my house,

chunks.en: he must do it anyway, because it is a rule of beis din.
chunks.st: he is nevertheless obligated as though he had written it, as it is a stipulation of the court.

chunks.en: This is how the people of Yerushalayim wrote.
chunks.st: The mishna comments: The residents of Jerusalem would write in this manner,

chunks.he: אַנְשֵׁי גָלִיל הָיוּ כוֹתְבִין כְּאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלָיִם.
chunks.en: The people of the Galil wrote like the people of Yerushalayim.

chunks.st: In contrast, the residents of Judea would write:

chunks.en: until the heirs want to give you your kesubah.
chunks.st: Until the heirs want to give you your marriage contract.

chunks.en: So if the heirs want,
chunks.st: Consequently, if the heirs wish,

chunks.en: they give her the kesubah and let her go.
chunks.st: they may give her marriage contract to her and release her,
chunks.stMore: and she must find her own living arrangements and provide for herself.
